questions.key_step: Write g piecewise on (-2,2) and compare one-sided derivatives at 0 and 1.
questions.justification: Routine piecewise construction with modulus; single kink to find. Chain of 3-4 standard steps, no insight (L2).

questions.key_step: Simplify f(g(x)) = x/(x-1); one-one, range misses 1.
questions.justification: One standard Mobius simplification and a range check (L1).

questions.key_step: Compare -|x| with -sqrt(1-x^2) and count kinks incl. the crossing points.
questions.justification: Standard max-of-two-curves sketch; three points to locate (L2).

questions.key_step: Subtract consecutive relations to get (n+1)f(n+1)=nf(n), so nf(n) is constant.
questions.justification: Standard difference trick, then evaluate f(2) and substitute (L2).

questions.key_step: On each [k,k+1) f is k/(1+x^2), decreasing; union of four half-open intervals is contiguous.
questions.justification: Four pieces, endpoint comparison; precision with open/closed ends (L2).

questions.key_step: Put x=tan(theta): the equation becomes pi/2-2theta = 2theta.
questions.justification: Standard substitution plus domain check of principal values (L2).

questions.key_step: [x] and [x/4] both jump by 1 at x=4, so they cancel.
questions.justification: One-sided limits of two greatest-integer terms; single step (L1).

questions.key_step: Intersect the domains and exclude x=0 and x=1 where quotients are undefined.
questions.justification: Single domain-intersection idea (L1).

questions.key_step: f(f(x))=x for all x forces a=1 after clearing denominators.
questions.justification: Algebraic simplification of a composite then identity in x (L2).

questions.key_step: Reduce to [x]-[2x]=7 and solve on the two halves of each unit interval, then exclude endpoints of non-existence.
questions.justification: Greatest-integer limit with half-integer breakpoints and endpoint decisions (L3); options check.

questions.key_step: x lies between n(C)+n(T)-100 and min(n(C),n(T)).
questions.justification: One inclusion-exclusion bound (L1).

questions.key_step: Even part of a^x is (a^x+a^-x)/2; expand f1(x+y)+f1(x-y).
questions.justification: Identify even part, then product-to-sum expansion (L2).

questions.key_step: Exponent 3/2 > 1 forces f'(y)=0, so f is constant.
questions.justification: Short solution but the 'Holder exponent >1' idea is not practised often (L3).

questions.key_step: Test the three properties with explicit irrational examples; fails symmetry and transitivity.
questions.justification: Property checks with irrational counterexamples; routine (L2); +0.5 for equivalence relation.
One identity applied once (L1).

questions.key_step: For x<0 near 0: [x]=-1, |x|=-x; substitute and cancel.
questions.justification: Single one-sided evaluation (L1).

questions.key_step: Take sine of both sides, solve, and verify roots against principal-value domains.
questions.justification: Squaring step with extraneous-root check; several stages (L3).

questions.key_step: Build irrational numbers whose squares sum to rational/irrational so a chain a R b R c fails; transitivity of two relations.
questions.justification: Needs inventive irrational constructions for two relations, each checked (L3); +0.5 for relations.

questions.key_step: tan^-1 a + tan^-1 b = pi/4 gives (1+a)(1+b)=2; the series is ln(1+a)+ln(1+b).
questions.justification: Two standard facts chained (L2).
Nested modulus kinks; standard (L2).
